prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Greenvale Metro’s Communications-Based Train Control (CBTC) system serves underground/surface railway in peak, off-peak, and engineering-hour patterns; objectives: safety, advertised headway, predictable dwell, rapid recovery. Control room handles strategic regulation; train/wayside functions tactical protection.
Line Traffic Controller monitors service, authorizes operational changes, coordinates incidents/recovery. Revenue Train Operator owns readiness, cab/passenger procedures, instruction compliance. Voice Dispatch Console supports fallback coordination with these actors and field staff.
Metro Operations Control System (Lantern) supplies positions, regulation, alarms, command interfaces; sends Crew Login Token Bundle for controlled duty start. Service Timetable Server supplies regulation plans; Passenger Information Gateway distributes approved customer messages.
North District Zone Controller and South District Zone Controller calculate movement authorities from train location reports, occupancy, field states. East Junction Interlocking and West Junction Interlocking control vital points/signals, accepting only safety-compliant commands; indications reach onboard through safety channels.
Atlas Onboard Controller (drawing alias Kestrel) activates after operator authentication, train energization, valid integrity indications; supervises protection, authority processing, speed enforcement, door enable, train-interface commands. Safety-critical states: initialization, protected manual operation, automatic train operation, fallback operation, cutout. Received authorities require sequence/applicability/consistency checks.
Dual Channel Odometer supplies independent speed/distance measurements from axle rotation, inertial sensing, calibration; onboard compares channels continuously, degrading mode above divergence threshold.
Train Radio Modem connects trains to Wayside Radio Access Network. Safety Data Communication Network carries approved safety messages with deterministic performance, segregation, monitored availability. Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges platform indications to coordinate movements/doors.
Normal operation automatically regulates headways/separation, presenting exceptions. Degraded operation requires rulebook-defined safe state, reduced automation, human confirmation, conservative movements. Location-confidence/communications loss or vital disagreement restricts movement pending resolution/approved procedure.
Signal Maintenance Engineer (Maple) uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server for health/alarm/restoration support without bypassing authority. Cyber Security Officer oversees access, key management via Cryptographic Key Management Appliance, and availability/integrity-related security response.

New part:
S033: When odometry confidence is reduced, the onboard functions increase position uncertainty and request operating actions that preserve separation from other trains.
S034: The trainborne interface to propulsion and braking equipment converts safety commands into vehicle-compatible requests while preserving electrical isolation from non-vital circuits.
S035: Brake assurance functions verify service and emergency brake availability by monitoring brake feedback, pneumatic pressure indications, and commanded deceleration response.
S036: During each enforcement cycle, Atlas Onboard Controller recalculates the braking demand needed to keep the train within the authorized movement limits.
S037: Atlas Onboard Controller produces the Brake Curve Checksum Log after validating the active enforcement data set.
S038: Train Radio Modem provides the onboard data radio function and maintains CBTC sessions over Wayside Radio Access Network coverage areas.
S039: The radio subsystem reports link quality, registration state, and session continuity information to Atlas Onboard Controller for use in mode management.
S040: Safety Data Communication Network provides the protected communications transport used by train control messages that require integrity, authentication, and bounded latency.
S041: Safety Data Communication Network sends the Clock Drift Sample Report at defined synchronization intervals.
S042: Cryptographic Key Management Appliance supports the security material used by onboard communications without changing the safety logic executed on the train.
S043: The operator interface presents movement authority limits, permitted speed, train location confidence, radio condition, and required operator actions to Revenue Train Operator.
S044: Acknowledgements entered by Revenue Train Operator are passed to Atlas Onboard Controller through a monitored input path that rejects stale or inconsistent commands.
S045: Voice Dispatch Console remains operationally separate from the vital CBTC data path, but it provides a means for voice coordination during degraded service.
S046: Platform Screen Door Controller exchanges door enable and closed-and-locked indications with the train interface when the train is correctly berthed at a platform.
S047: Passenger Information Gateway receives non-vital train position and service state data through an interface that prevents passenger systems from influencing safety decisions.
S048: Service Timetable Server provides schedule context to Metro Operations Control System and related non-vital functions, while onboard enforcement remains based on safety authority and train state.
S049: The Maintenance Diagnostic Server is referred to in some maintenance work instructions as Quarry, but this document uses Maintenance Diagnostic Server as the canonical name.
S050: Maintenance Diagnostic Server collects non-vital health indications from trainborne equipment so that Signal Maintenance Engineer can review faults without connecting directly to vital processing functions.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
